rows.recommendation: In HFrEF, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists are recommended for eligible patients (adequate kidney function and potassium). Potassium and kidney function should be checked when starting and regularly afterwards.
rows.patient_text: This medicine helps your heart work better, but it can raise potassium. Regular blood tests keep it safe.

rows.recommendation: Drugs that cause fluid retention or worsen heart function, such as NSAIDs, should be avoided in patients with heart failure when possible.
rows.patient_text: Common pain medicines like ibuprofen and naproxen can make heart failure worse. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about safer options.

rows.recommendation: Diltiazem and verapamil can weaken heart contraction and are considered potentially harmful in HFrEF.
rows.patient_text: Some blood pressure and heart rhythm medicines are not recommended for your type of heart failure. Your doctor can confirm if yours is appropriate.

rows.recommendation: Patients should weigh themselves daily and know when weight gain should prompt contact with their care team, as part of heart failure self-care.
rows.patient_text: Weigh yourself every morning. Fast weight gain can mean fluid build-up, even before you feel worse.

rows.recommendation: Avoiding excessive sodium is reasonable in heart failure; trial evidence (SODIUM-HF) did not show fewer clinical events with stricter restriction, so messaging should avoid extreme limits.
rows.patient_text: Try to avoid very salty foods. Your care team can tell you what level is right for you.

rows.topic: SGLT2 inhibitors across the EF spectrum
rows.recommendation: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalization and are recommended in HFrEF and reasonable in HFpEF per current U.S. documents; check updates in the 2026 HFpEF pathway.
rows.patient_text: This medicine can lower the chance of being hospitalized for heart failure, whether or not you have diabetes.
